fatal_errors: The proposed intervention—severe plastic deformation of conventional stainless steel—does not reconstruct the AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating, atmospheric plasma spraying, or 550 °C annealing central to the target.
The proposed chloride-solution study omits the target's 3.5 wt% sulfuric-acid exposure and 900 °C cyclic Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 hot-corrosion conditions.
explanation: This is a scientifically plausible alternative hypothesis rather than a reconstruction of the target study. It aligns broadly with the corrosion-resistance problem and partially overlaps mechanistically through grain refinement, chromium enrichment, passivation, polarization, and impedance measurements. Its same-composition coarse-grained control, film-composition analysis, and explicit falsification rule are sound, although SPD can also alter residual stress, defect density, texture, and phase state, so grain-boundary-mediated chromium diffusion is not uniquely isolated. Evidence E1 directly supports improved passivation and chromium enrichment in ultrafine-grained stainless steels, while E2 concerns sacrificial Al and molten-salt redox behavior in a different HEA and provides little support for the stated grain-boundary mechanism. The boundaries are qualitative and nuclear-service conditions are underspecified. Most importantly, the generated account misses the target material architecture, processing window, phase evolution, Al/Cr-rich protective scales, and high-temperature molten-salt degradation mechanism.
